hpi: Obstetric/Gestational Hypertension: Clinical Presentation and Management. Gestational hypertension is defined as new-onset hypertension after 20 weeks of gestation. The patient should be monitored closely for signs of preeclampsia. The treatment for gestational hypertension includes monitoring blood pressure and, if necessary, initiating antihypertensive therapy. It is important to note that the patient should be counseled regarding the potential risks associated with gestational hypertension and the need for close follow-up. The management of gestational hypertension may include lifestyle modifications and, in some cases, medication.
